description: design the two oligos for Golden Gate EIPCR site-directed mutagenesis — saturating a site into a library with degenerate codes, or making a single defined clone — then simulate the construction file and confirm the product is the right size with the mutation in the right place
phrases: design oligos to mutate a site
make a saturation library at this position
design a library oligo with NNNN
how do I mutate 4 bases in this plasmid
make a point mutant of this plasmid
which type IIS enzyme can I use on this plasmid

requires.note: findanneal — scores GC clamp, GC content, base balance and randomness over 18-25 nt
parseCF and simCF — the only thing that decides whether a design is good

returns: every design C6 confirms, best first: the enzyme, the 4 bp overhang and which side of the window it sits on, the forward and reverse oligos, and the verified product size with the sequence context around the mutation. Designs C6 will not build are returned separately with the reason
notes: JCA's procedure, 2026-09-10. Start from the template, model the mutant by replacing the window with degeneracy codes, choose a 4 bp overhang 1-5 bp AWAY from that window — never abutting it, because a sticky end beside an N biases which variants ligate and the skew cannot be told from biology afterwards; a flush overhang is fine for a single clone. The overhang may fall either side of the window and both are tried. Annealing regions come from C6's findanneal with the 5' end locked, not from a length rule. The enzyme is the first in BsaI, BsmBI, BbsI, BseRI, AarI, SapI whose site is absent from the template on either strand. Oligos are ccaaa + site + a + the fixed part + the annealing region. Nothing is reported until simCF has built it and the product has both the right length and the replacement sitting against the base that followed the window — a design that simulates to the wrong size is worse than one that fails, because it would be ordered.
